Package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.classic.remote

Class RemoteUrlPolicyState

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.client.classic.remote.RemoteUrlPolicyState
public final class RemoteUrlPolicyState extends Object
Marks the current thread as executing an SSRF-guard-active @Remote call, for the duration of one blocking RestRequest.run() (including any internal retries/redirect hops it triggers on the same thread).

The classic engine shares a single CloseableHttpClient across every request the client issues, whether @Remote-originated or an ordinary client.get(url) call. Since neither Apache HttpClient's HttpClientConnectionManager.requestConnection SPI nor its RedirectStrategy SPI receives enough information to distinguish which caller triggered a given connection lease or redirect decision, this thread-local flag is set for the duration of exactly one @Remote invocation (which runs synchronously, blocking the calling thread, per Juneau's classic-engine execution model). While it is set, the client's connection manager leases connections from a dedicated pool whose connections are all opened through the org.apache.juneau.http.remote.RemoteUrlPolicy pin, and its redirect strategy defers 3xx handling to Juneau's revalidating redirect loop — leaving ordinary (non-@Remote) requests on the same client, and their separate pool, completely unaffected.

The guard of the @Remote request itself also travels on the request's HttpContext, so it holds even when the request is executed on another thread; this flag additionally guards any other request made on the calling thread while the call runs.

Since:
10.0.0

  • Method Details

    • activate

      public static void activate()
      Marks the calling thread as executing an SSRF-guard-active @Remote call.

      Callers must invoke deactivate() in a finally block once the call (including any retries) has completed. Calls nest: the thread stays marked until every activate() has been matched by a deactivate(), so a guarded call made while another one is running does not end the outer call's guard.

    • deactivate

      public static void deactivate()
      Ends one activate(); the calling thread's marker is cleared when the outermost guarded call ends.

    • isActive

      public static boolean isActive()

      Returns:
      true if the guard is active on this thread.
